entries.definition: A family of cooperative ant-based optimization algorithms that learns shared edge desirabilities using Q-learning-inspired next-state estimates and delayed reinforcement from completed solutions.
entries.identity_notes: This record denotes the Ant-Q family through its traveling-salesman formulations, especially pseudo-random-proportional construction and best-tour reinforcement. Its next-state estimate distinguishes the nondegenerate Ant-Q update from the selected ACS rule targeting a constant tau0. The authors relate Ant System to the broader family; that relationship does not make every Ant-Q configuration identical to Ant System. This is an algorithm-family concept, not a trained value function or a proof of Q-learning equivalence. limitations: The eligible action set depends on an ant’s visited-city history, while AQ is shared per edge. City identity alone is therefore not a complete Markov state for tour feasibility. The 1995 conclusion treats transfer of Q-learning theory as future work; standard Q-learning convergence is not an established Ant-Q guarantee here.

The 1995 generic diagram loops over edges to compute delayed reinforcement and gives an incompletely specified final update domain; its repeat jump omits explicit state reset and its terminal local maximum needs a convention. The 1996 method makes best-tour-only global updates and per-tour reset explicit but references its update equation without restating the earlier zero-next-state convention. The record preserves these version details instead of claiming a fully executable common pseudocode.

The pseudo-random, pseudo-random-proportional and random-proportional construction rules are distinct members. Positive trails alone do not ensure exploration when q0=1, candidates are excluded or weights vanish. Empty eligible sets, zero distances, ties, repeated edge updates and numerical underflow require explicit handling.

The learned edge values guide stochastic search rather than certify globally optimal tours. Heuristic choice, parameters, number of ants, update ordering and stopping affect results. Neither the paper’s observed noncollapse nor its TSP/ATSP comparisons is asserted as a universal guarantee.

claims.statement: Maintain shared positive AQ(r,s) edge values, a heuristic HE(r,s) such as inverse positive distance, and each ant’s set J of unvisited cities. In the pseudo-random-proportional variant, draw q uniformly in [0,1]: for q<=q0 choose an eligible edge maximizing AQ^delta*HE^beta, otherwise sample with probabilities proportional to those weights over eligible cities. While constructing tours, the displayed update is AQ(r,s)_new=(1−alpha)*AQ(r,s)+alpha*(DeltaAQ(r,s)+gamma*max_{z in J(s)} AQ(s,z)); immediate DeltaAQ is zero in the inspected variants. After completing tours, delayed reinforcement is W/L_best on edges of a selected best tour and zero elsewhere. The paper studies both iteration-best and best-so-far choices and selects iteration-best for most subsequent experiments. In the 1995 Figure1 delayed phase, the next-state term is explicitly declared zero, so the per-edge update where applied reduces to (1−alpha)*AQ+alpha*DeltaAQ. The 1996 presentation explicitly restricts that global phase to the iteration-best tour and resets per-tour ant state each iteration. These are source-scoped formulations; terminal handling and the exact edge-update schedule must be declared when implementing a concrete member.

entries.name: Population-based incremental learning
entries.definition: An optimization method that samples candidate solutions from a probability-vector representation and incrementally moves that representation toward high-evaluation sampled solutions, with probability-vector mutation in its basic formulation.
entries.identity_notes: The inspected baseline uses independent Bernoulli coordinates for fixed-length binary solutions and moves toward the current generation’s single best sample. Multiple-positive and negative-example updates are explicit extensions. It is not continual learning, supervised classification, direct crossover of persistent chromosomes, or the general cross-entropy optimization framework. A single-elite Bernoulli CE fit with smoothing can coincide with the PBIL attraction step; that shared subcase does not establish equivalence of the full named procedures. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 291 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 61 and 71 lines respectively. Text hits were prior candidate leads, citations to a reused Ant System source, neighboring mechanism distinctions, saved review/report material, and unrelated PBIL strings in ignored HOGENOM prefix-map URLs. Eight exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and five native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The product of coordinate marginals cannot represent general dependencies between bits or arbitrary mixtures of dissimilar good solutions. Different populations can have the same marginals; representation and encoding affect the search.

A high learning rate can concentrate probabilities prematurely; a very low rate can make adaptation slow. With interior probabilities and 0<LR<1, a finite attraction step stays interior in exact arithmetic, but this does not guarantee lasting exploration or a finite-budget global optimum. Mutation events can be absent, and floating-point probabilities can collapse.

Probability-vector mutation is not a bit flip of every sampled chromosome and is not guaranteed to increase diversity on each event: a move toward an already favored endpoint can increase concentration. Mutation toward .5 is discussed separately as a future alternative.

Selection of the current-generation winner depends on objective ordering, whereas tie handling, objective direction, noise, population size and mutation randomization remain configuration choices. A preserved output archive does not force that archived vector into future samples. The report’s comparative results are not universal performance guarantees.

claims.statement: Initialize each binary-coordinate probability P_i to .5. At each generation, independently sample a population of binary vectors according to P, evaluate them and choose a sample x_best with the highest objective value in that generation. Update each coordinate P_i_new=(1−LR)*P_i+LR*x_best_i. Then, with a configured mutation probability per coordinate, shift that probability toward a randomly chosen binary endpoint b using P_i_new=(1−MUT_SHIFT)*P_i+MUT_SHIFT*b. Repeat for the selected budget or stopping rule. For these convex-update interpretations, LR and MUT_SHIFT lie in [0,1]. Maintain the highest-evaluation solution vectors separately for return, as the Figure4 caption recommends. The baseline updates its distribution toward the current-generation winner, not automatically the best-so-far archive. Injecting the archived best into later populations, moving toward several winners, or learning away from differing bits of poor samples are separately described extensions.

entries.name: Rank-based Ant System
entries.definition: An Ant System variant that weights pheromone deposits from a selected number of the current iteration’s best tours by rank and adds a separate reinforced contribution from the best-so-far tour.
entries.identity_notes: This record denotes ASrank in the inspected 1997 working paper. It differs from unweighted all-ant deposits, elitist Ant System’s all-ant-plus-archive deposits, and MAX–MIN’s single-best bounded-trail update. Rank determines which ants contribute and their additional weights, but inverse tour length remains in the deposit; the rule is not purely ordinal. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 291 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 61 and 71 lines respectively. Text hits were prior candidate leads, citations to a reused Ant System source, neighboring mechanism distinctions, saved review/report material, and unrelated PBIL strings in ignored HOGENOM prefix-map URLs. limitations: The displayed sum requires enough current ants and a declared integer sigma; sigma=1 leaves only the best-so-far contribution. Ties in tour length need a rank assignment or tie policy, which can matter when tied tours use different edges.

Rank weighting still multiplies inverse positive tour cost. An increasing transformation or constant shift of costs can preserve ranks while changing deposits, heuristic weights and the search trajectory. Calling the algorithm rank-based does not establish invariance to arbitrary fitness transformations.

The retained best tour is a search memory, not a certified optimum. Strong elite weighting and vanishing trails can reduce exploration. Evaporation and rank selection do not provide the positive support bounds of MAX–MIN, and no finite-run global-optimality guarantee is asserted.

claims.statement: Construct traveling-salesman tours using Ant System’s feasible-city probabilities proportional to tau^alpha*eta^beta with eta=1/d, and retain the best-so-far tour. Sort the m current tours by nondecreasing positive length L_1<=...<=L_m. In the displayed rule choose an integer elite weight sigma with 1<=sigma<=m+1, so the top sigma−1 current tours are available. Update each edge by rho*tau plus the sum, over ranks mu=1..sigma−1 whose tours use the edge, of (sigma−mu)*Q/L_mu, plus sigma*Q/L_best if the best-so-far tour uses that edge. Rho is trail retention, so 1−rho is the evaporated fraction. The archive contribution is added separately even when the same tour also contributes through a current rank. Reconstruct new tours using the resulting trails for the next iteration; the paper’s update does not add MAX–MIN trail bounds or the ACS local rule.

entries.name: Elitist Ant System
entries.definition: An Ant System variant that retains the standard all-ant pheromone deposits and adds extra reinforcement to edges of the best-so-far tour after each construction cycle.
entries.identity_notes: The defining change is active extra reinforcement of the best-so-far tour, beyond merely remembering or returning it. The original Ant System paper describes the elitist strategy and the 1997 rank-based study names it ASelite with an explicit equation. It differs from rank selection, which can omit lower-ranked current contributions, and from single-best-only updates. Zero elite weight recovers the base update as a limiting configuration. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 291 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 61 and 71 lines respectively. Text hits were prior candidate leads, citations to a reused Ant System source, neighboring mechanism distinctions, saved review/report material, and unrelated PBIL strings in ignored HOGENOM prefix-map URLs. Eight exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and five native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The method assumes valid positive-cost tours and well-defined inverse-distance construction weights. Extra elite reinforcement biases future sampling; it does not force future ants to take the archived tour or guarantee that its edges are globally optimal.

The original study explicitly reports premature concentration when elite reinforcement is too strong in its tested setting. A favorable elite count on one TSP instance is not a universal parameter recommendation or a convergence theorem.

This mechanism is not the same as copying a best chromosome unchanged into a genetic population, nor merely storing a best-so-far output. It retains every ant’s ordinary deposit; rank-based selection can truncate current contributions and single-best-only reinforcement omits the all-ant term.

claims.statement: In the inspected positive-distance traveling-salesman formulation, place m ants at starting cities and initialize pheromone trails. claims.statement: Construct solutions by choosing feasible components with probabilities proportional to tau^alpha*eta^beta, as in Ant System. For positive-cost minimization, select one iteration-best or best-so-far solution according to the declared reinforcement schedule. Evaporate every trail using retention rho and add 1/f(best) only to components of that selected solution, with zero deposit elsewhere. Clip the resulting trails to [tau_min,tau_max] after each iteration. The source initializes trails at a high value that is brought to the upper limit; this preserves initial exploration pressure relative to low trails. Its upper-limit estimate is tau_max=1/((1−rho)*f(best_so_far)), updated when the best cost improves. For the source’s TSP lower-limit heuristic, n is the number of cities and avg=n/2 approximates the number of choices at each step. The displayed formula uses unit pheromone exponent alpha=1, equal decision probabilities and negligible heuristic differences: with p_dec=p_best^(1/n), tau_min=tau_max*(1−p_dec)/((avg−1)*p_dec), capped at tau_max if larger. This is an approximate configuration rule, not the exact probability of reconstructing a real tour. Positive limits, 0<=rho<1, a valid denominator and declared handling of boundary parameters are required for this account.
